title: 2 Samuel Chapter 22 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 2 Samuel chapter 22 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 2 Samuel Chapter 22 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 2 Samuel Chapter 22.

questions.question: Who spoke the words of the song in 2 Samuel 22?
questions.correctAnswer: David
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 22:1 states that David spoke unto the LORD the words of this song.

questions.question: In 2 Samuel 22:2, what does David call the LORD?
questions.correctAnswer: Rock, fortress, deliverer
questions.explanation: Verse 2 describes the LORD as David's rock, fortress, and deliverer.

questions.question: According to 2 Samuel 22:3, which of the following is NOT a title David gives to God?
questions.correctAnswer: Judge of nations
questions.explanation: Verse 3 lists shield, horn of salvation, high tower, refuge, and savior, but not judge of nations.

questions.question: What does David say he will do in 2 Samuel 22:4 to be saved from his enemies?
questions.correctAnswer: Call on the LORD
questions.explanation: Verse 4 says David will call on the LORD, who is worthy to be praised, to be saved from his enemies.

questions.question: In 2 Samuel 22:5, what caused David to be afraid?
questions.correctAnswer: Floods of ungodly men
questions.explanation: Verse 5 mentions that the floods of ungodly men made David afraid.

questions.question: True or False: In 2 Samuel 22:6, David says the snares of death prevented him.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Verse 6 clearly states that the snares of death prevented him.

questions.question: How did God respond to David's cry for help according to 2 Samuel 22:7?
options: He heard his voice out of his temple
questions.correctAnswer: He heard his voice out of his temple
questions.explanation: Verse 7 states that God heard David's voice out of his temple and his cry entered into his ears.

questions.question: What happened to the earth and the foundations of heaven in 2 Samuel 22:8?
questions.correctAnswer: They shook and trembled
questions.explanation: Verse 8 says the earth shook and trembled; the foundations of heaven moved and shook because God was wroth.

questions.question: True or False: According to 2 Samuel 22:9, fire came out of God's mouth and coals were kindled.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Verse 9 mentions that fire came out of God's mouth and coals were kindled.

questions.question: In 2 Samuel 22:11, upon what did the LORD ride?
questions.correctAnswer: Cherub
questions.explanation: Verse 11 says the LORD rode upon a cherub and was seen upon the wings of the wind.

questions.question: What did the LORD make around Him according to 2 Samuel 22:12?
options: Darkness pavilions, dark waters, and thick clouds
questions.correctAnswer: Darkness pavilions, dark waters, and thick clouds
questions.explanation: Verse 12 describes the LORD making darkness pavilions, dark waters, and thick clouds of the skies around Him.

questions.question: According to 2 Samuel 22:14, what did the LORD do from heaven?
questions.correctAnswer: Thundered
questions.explanation: Verse 14 states that the LORD thundered from heaven and the most High uttered his voice.

questions.question: What appeared at the rebuking of the LORD in 2 Samuel 22:16?
options: Channels of the sea and foundations of the world
questions.correctAnswer: Channels of the sea and foundations of the world
questions.explanation: Verse 16 says that channels of the sea appeared and foundations of the world were discovered at the rebuking of the LORD.

questions.question: True or False: In 2 Samuel 22, David says the LORD delivered him because He was angry with him.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: The chapter does not say the LORD delivered David because He was angry; rather, it shows deliverance because of God's help and delight (e.g., verses 19-20).

questions.question: In what order do these events appear in 2 Samuel 22:8-11? 1) The earth shook, 2) Fire came out of God's mouth, 3) God rode upon a cherub, 4) God bowed the heavens and came down.
questions.explanation: Verse 8: earth shook (1); verse 9: fire from mouth (2); verse 10: bowed heavens and came down (4); verse 11: rode upon cherub (3).

medium.title: 2 Samuel Chapter 22 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 2 Samuel Chapter 22 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to 2 Samuel 22:18, why did the LORD deliver David from his strong enemy and those who hated him?
options: Because they were too strong for him
Because David was a mighty warrior
questions.correctAnswer: Because they were too strong for him
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 22:18 states that David's enemies were too strong for him, so the LORD delivered him. This shows God's power in protecting those who are vulnerable. This is supported by verses 19 and 20 that emphasize the LORD as David's stay and deliverer.

questions.question: What role does the LORD play in David's time of calamity according to 2 Samuel 22:19?
questions.correctAnswer: His stay
questions.explanation: Verse 19 describes the LORD as David's stay during calamity, implying that God is the source of support and stability in distressful times, complementing verse 18 where God delivers him from enemies.

questions.question: How does 2 Samuel 22:20 explain the LORD's motivation for delivering David?
options: Because the LORD delighted in him
questions.correctAnswer: Because the LORD delighted in him
questions.explanation: Verse 20 specifically says the LORD delivered David because He delighted in him, showing God's personal care. This connects with verses 18 and 19, emphasizing God's intervention based on His favor.

questions.question: What does 2 Samuel 22:21 say about how the LORD rewarded David?
options: According to his righteousness and the cleanness of his hands
According to his wealth and power
questions.correctAnswer: According to his righteousness and the cleanness of his hands
questions.explanation: Verse 21 states that the LORD rewarded David according to his righteousness and cleanness, highlighting the importance of integrity and moral purity, which is supported by verses 22-24 about obedience and uprightness.

questions.question: Based on 2 Samuel 22:22-24, what is the relationship between David's obedience to God's ways and his moral standing?
options: David kept the ways of the LORD and remained upright, avoiding iniquity
David occasionally disobeyed but was forgiven
David struggled with obedience and often sinned
David was unaware of God's statutes
questions.correctAnswer: David kept the ways of the LORD and remained upright, avoiding iniquity
questions.explanation: Verses 22 to 24 emphasize David's consistent obedience and uprightness before God, showing that keeping God's ways results in moral integrity and favor, as seen also in verse 21.

questions.question: How does 2 Samuel 22:25-27 illustrate God's character toward different kinds of people?
options: God shows mercy to the merciful and purity to the pure, but unsavoury to the froward
God ignores the merciful and favors the proud
God treats all people the same regardless of behavior
God punishes the merciful and rewards the froward
questions.correctAnswer: God shows mercy to the merciful and purity to the pure, but unsavoury to the froward
questions.explanation: Verses 26 and 27 describe God’s reciprocal nature—He reflects the heart of the person, showing mercy or purity to those who embody these traits and unsavoury character to the froward, teaching about the importance of holiness and humility.

questions.question: According to 2 Samuel 22:28, what does God do for the afflicted and the haughty?
options: Saves the afflicted and brings down the haughty
Ignores both the afflicted and the haughty
Blesses the haughty and punishes the afflicted
Saves the haughty and punishes the afflicted
questions.correctAnswer: Saves the afflicted and brings down the haughty
questions.explanation: Verse 28 clearly states God’s concern for the afflicted by saving them, while His eyes are upon the proud to bring them down, illustrating God's justice and compassion.

questions.question: What metaphor does David use in 2 Samuel 22:29 to describe the LORD's guidance in darkness?
options: The LORD is his lamp and lightens his darkness
The LORD is a shield and fortress
The LORD is a sword and weapon
The LORD is a cloud and shadow
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD is his lamp and lightens his darkness
questions.explanation: Verse 29 uses the metaphor of the LORD as a lamp that illuminates darkness, symbolizing guidance and hope in times of trouble, connecting with the theme of God’s protection in earlier verses.

questions.question: How does 2 Samuel 22:30 describe the strength David receives from God in battle?
options: By God, David runs through a troop and leaps over a wall
David relies on his own strength and weapons
David uses strategy to defeat enemies
questions.correctAnswer: By God, David runs through a troop and leaps over a wall
questions.explanation: Verse 30 highlights that David’s military victories are empowered by God, symbolizing divine enablement for seemingly impossible feats, illustrating faith and reliance on God.

questions.question: What does 2 Samuel 22:31 reveal about the nature of God's way and His protection?
options: God's way is perfect; His word is tried; He is a buckler to those who trust Him
God's way is unpredictable and His word is untested
God offers no protection to those who trust Him
God's way is imperfect but His mercy endures
questions.correctAnswer: God's way is perfect; His word is tried; He is a buckler to those who trust Him
questions.explanation: Verse 31 emphasizes God's perfection and reliability, and that He protects those who trust in Him, reinforcing the importance of faith and obedience as taught in preceding verses.

questions.question: According to 2 Samuel 22:32, who is identified as the only true God and rock?
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD
questions.explanation: Verse 32 explicitly states that the LORD is the only true God and rock, affirming the monotheistic belief that God alone is the foundation and strength, consistent with earlier verses calling God a rock and fortress.

questions.question: What does 2 Samuel 22:33 say about God's role in David's strength and path?
options: God is David's strength and power and makes his way perfect
David's strength comes from his own skills
David's path is uncertain despite God's help
questions.correctAnswer: God is David's strength and power and makes his way perfect
questions.explanation: Verse 33 shows that God is the source of David’s strength and power, and He perfects David’s path, highlighting trust in God for guidance and success.

questions.question: How does 2 Samuel 22:34 describe the transformation God brings to David's feet and position?
options: God makes David’s feet like hinds' feet and sets him upon high places
God makes David’s feet heavy and keeps him low
David climbs by his own effort
questions.correctAnswer: God makes David’s feet like hinds' feet and sets him upon high places
questions.explanation: Verse 34 uses the imagery of sure-footedness and elevation to describe God’s empowerment and exaltation of David, symbolizing stability and victory in difficult terrain.

questions.question: What lesson about God's response to different behaviors is taught in 2 Samuel 22:26 and 2 Samuel 22:27?
options: God shows mercy and purity to those who are merciful and pure, but shows Himself unsavoury to the froward
God treats everyone the same regardless of behavior
God favors the proud over the humble
questions.correctAnswer: God shows mercy and purity to those who are merciful and pure, but shows Himself unsavoury to the froward
questions.explanation: These verses teach the biblical virtue that God reflects the character of people, rewarding mercy and purity but opposing perverseness, guiding believers to live uprightly.

questions.question: True or False: 2 Samuel 22:24 states that David kept himself from iniquity and was upright before the LORD.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Verse 24 clearly states that David was upright before God and kept himself from iniquity, demonstrating his commitment to holiness and obedience.

hard.title: 2 Samuel Chapter 22 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 2 Samuel Chapter 22.

questions.question: What skill does David say God taught his hands, enabling him to break a bow of steel?
questions.correctAnswer: To war
questions.explanation: According to 2 Samuel 22:35, God teaches David's hands to war, strengthening him so that a bow of steel is broken by his arms.

questions.question: What has David received from God that has made him great, as stated in 2 Samuel 22?
questions.correctAnswer: Shield of salvation and gentleness
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 22:36 states that God has given David the shield of salvation and that God's gentleness has made him great.

questions.question: How does David describe the enlargement of his steps by God?
options: So that his feet did not slip
So that he could run faster
So that he could jump higher
So that he could climb mountains
questions.correctAnswer: So that his feet did not slip
questions.explanation: In 2 Samuel 22:37, David says God has enlarged his steps so that his feet did not slip.

questions.question: What was David's attitude towards his enemies according to 2 Samuel 22?
options: He pursued and destroyed them without turning back
questions.correctAnswer: He pursued and destroyed them without turning back
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 22:38 records David saying he pursued his enemies, destroyed them, and did not turn until he had consumed them.

questions.question: From whom did God deliver David, as expressed in this chapter?
options: From his strong enemy and those who hated him
questions.correctAnswer: From his strong enemy and those who hated him
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 22:18 states God delivered David from his strong enemy and those who hated him.

questions.question: What title does David give God that emphasizes protection and salvation in verses 47 and 51?
questions.correctAnswer: Rock and tower of salvation
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 22:47 calls God 'my rock' and 22:51 calls Him 'the tower of salvation'. These titles emphasize God's protection and salvation.

questions.question: Which verse describes God as the one who avenges David and subdues his enemies?
questions.correctAnswer: 2 Samuel 22:48
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 22:48 specifically states, 'It is God that avengeth me, and that bringeth down the people under me.'

questions.question: What is the significance of the phrase 'He maketh my feet like hinds' feet' in 2 Samuel 22:34?
options: It symbolizes agility and surefootedness in difficult terrain
questions.correctAnswer: It symbolizes agility and surefootedness in difficult terrain
questions.explanation: The imagery of 'hinds' feet' in 2 Samuel 22:34 refers to the agility and surefootedness of a deer, implying God makes David able to navigate difficult places securely.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage is closely related to 2 Samuel 22 as a parallel song of praise by David?
questions.correctAnswer: Psalm 18
questions.explanation: Psalm 18 is a parallel poetic song of praise by David with many similar themes and wording to 2 Samuel 22, reflecting God's deliverance and protection.

questions.question: What literary device is prominently used throughout 2 Samuel 22 to emphasize God's protection and power?
questions.correctAnswer: Parallelism
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 22 employs parallelism, a common Hebrew poetic device, by repeating and contrasting phrases to emphasize God's attributes and actions (e.g., verses 2-4).

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word translated as 'rock' (Hebrew: 'tsur') symbolize in this chapter?
questions.correctAnswer: Strength, stability, and refuge
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'tsur' (rock) used in verses like 2 Samuel 22:2 symbolizes God's strength, stability, and refuge for David.

questions.question: According to 2 Samuel 22:42, how did the enemies react when they looked for help?
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Verse 42 says the enemies looked for help but found none, even to the LORD, who did not answer them, confirming the truth of this statement.

questions.question: David claims that strangers will fear and fade away from their hiding places according to 2 Samuel 22:46.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 22:46 states that strangers shall fade away and be afraid out of their close places, so this statement is true.

questions.question: In 2 Samuel 22:31, which phrase describes how God's way is characterized?
questions.correctAnswer: Perfect and tried
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 22:31 states that God's way is perfect and His word is tried, emphasizing God's reliability and holiness.

questions.question: What does David say God has given him to enable him to fight and defeat his enemies in 2 Samuel 22:40?
questions.correctAnswer: Strength to battle
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 22:40 says God girded David with strength for battle, enabling him to subdue his enemies.

theological.title: 2 Samuel Chapter 22 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 2 Samuel Chapter 22 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What divine attribute is primarily emphasized in 2 Samuel 22:2 when David calls the LORD his rock and fortress?
questions.correctAnswer: God's immutability and strength
questions.explanation: Verse 2 describes the LORD as rock and fortress, metaphors emphasizing God's unchanging nature and strength as a protector.

questions.question: According to 2 Samuel 22:7, what demonstrates God's attentiveness to human suffering?
options: He hears and responds to the cries of distress
He sends angels to fight battles
questions.correctAnswer: He hears and responds to the cries of distress
questions.explanation: Verse 7 says David called upon the LORD in distress and God heard his voice and his cry entered into His ears, showing divine responsiveness.

questions.question: What theological truth about God's sovereignty is depicted in 2 Samuel 22:8-9 with the earth shaking and fire from His mouth?
options: God exercises cosmic power in judgment
God is limited by natural laws
God is indifferent to human affairs
God only acts through human agents
questions.correctAnswer: God exercises cosmic power in judgment
questions.explanation: These verses illustrate God's wrath causing cosmic disturbances and consuming fire, affirming His sovereign power over creation and judgment.

questions.question: In 2 Samuel 22:11, God is described as riding upon a cherub and flying on wings of the wind. What does this imagery primarily reveal about God?
options: His transcendent mobility and divine majesty
His dependence on angels for power
questions.correctAnswer: His transcendent mobility and divine majesty
questions.explanation: Verse 11 uses the imagery of cherubs and wings of wind to express God's majestic and sovereign transcendence beyond physical bounds.

questions.question: How does 2 Samuel 22:17-18 contribute to the doctrine of God's deliverance?
options: God actively rescues His people from overwhelming enemies
God only delivers after human effort
God's deliverance is symbolic, not real
questions.correctAnswer: God actively rescues His people from overwhelming enemies
questions.explanation: These verses affirm God taking David from many waters and delivering him from strong enemies, showing God’s active saving power.

questions.question: What does 2 Samuel 22:21-24 teach about the relationship between righteousness and divine reward?
options: God rewards according to righteousness and faithfulness
God rewards arbitrarily without regard to conduct
Righteousness has no impact on divine favor
questions.correctAnswer: God rewards according to righteousness and faithfulness
questions.explanation: David states the LORD rewarded him according to his righteousness and cleanness, indicating divine justice aligned with moral conduct.

questions.question: Which attribute of God is highlighted in 2 Samuel 22:26-27 regarding His response to different human characters?
questions.correctAnswer: God's justice and holiness
questions.explanation: These verses portray God as merciful to the merciful, pure to the pure, and unsavory to the froward, revealing His just and holy nature.

questions.question: How does 2 Samuel 22:29 illustrate God's role in the believer's life?
options: God is the source of guidance and illumination
questions.correctAnswer: God is the source of guidance and illumination
questions.explanation: Calling the LORD 'my lamp' and the one who lightens darkness shows God as the believer’s guide and source of spiritual illumination.

questions.question: What combined doctrinal insight do verses 30 and 31 provide about divine empowerment and protection?
options: God enables victory and provides perfect protection for those who trust Him
Victory is independent of divine assistance
questions.correctAnswer: God enables victory and provides perfect protection for those who trust Him
questions.explanation: Verse 30 describes running through troops and leaping over walls by God’s help; verse 31 calls God a perfect way and buckler for trusters, showing divine empowerment and protection.

questions.question: How do verses 33-35 depict God's role in sanctification and spiritual warfare?
options: God strengthens and equips the believer for spiritual battle
God leaves believers to fight alone
God’s power is only for physical battles
questions.correctAnswer: God strengthens and equips the believer for spiritual battle
questions.explanation: These verses declare God as strength and power who perfects the way and teaches hands to war, equipping believers for spiritual and physical warfare.

questions.question: What theological doctrine is emphasized by the imagery in 2 Samuel 22:36-37 about gentleness and enlarged steps?
options: Sanctification as God’s gentle empowerment and stability
questions.correctAnswer: Sanctification as God’s gentle empowerment and stability
questions.explanation: God’s gentleness making David great and enlarging his steps shows divine grace enabling spiritual growth and stability.

questions.question: What does 2 Samuel 22:44-45 teach about God's sovereign rule over nations and peoples?
options: God raises unknown peoples to serve His anointed king
God is indifferent to foreign nations
questions.correctAnswer: God raises unknown peoples to serve His anointed king
questions.explanation: These verses describe strangers submitting and serving David, showing God’s sovereign control extending beyond Israel.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that God is silent and uninvolved in human conflict. What does 2 Samuel 22:40-42 actually teach about God’s involvement in battle?
options: God girds the believer with strength and subdues enemies
God favors the strongest human armies
questions.correctAnswer: God girds the believer with strength and subdues enemies
questions.explanation: Verses 40-42 explain that God gives strength to battle and subdues those who oppose, disproving claims of divine silence or passivity.

questions.question: What combined theological truth emerges from 2 Samuel 22:47 and 2 Samuel 22:51 about God's eternal kingship and mercy?
options: God is exalted as the eternal rock and merciful tower for His anointed forever
God’s mercy is limited to David’s lifetime
God is only a warrior, not merciful
questions.correctAnswer: God is exalted as the eternal rock and merciful tower for His anointed forever
questions.explanation: Verse 47 praises God as rock and salvation; verse 51 calls Him tower of salvation showing mercy to David and his seed forever, combining eternal kingship and mercy.

questions.question: How does 2 Samuel 22:3-4 synthesize the doctrine of salvation and worship?
options: Trusting God as savior leads to calling on Him in praise and deliverance
Worship is only for the righteous
questions.correctAnswer: Trusting God as savior leads to calling on Him in praise and deliverance
questions.explanation: Verse 3 describes God as shield and savior to trust; verse 4 emphasizes calling on the LORD worthy to be praised for salvation, linking trust, worship, and deliverance.
